..
Issued at 412 PM CDT Wed Sep 23 2026

Currently...

Have had a bit of a lull in shower activity through much of the
day, following some spotty precipitation that crossed over 
northern portions of the forecast area late last night into 
early this morning. Another wave of increased mid-upper lift is 
bringing the next batch of scattered activity in from the SSW 
here at mid-afternoon. Flow across the Central Plains remains 
southwesterly today...upper air and satellite data showing high 
pressure centered generally over the eastern Srn Plains/western 
Gulf Coast region and northward extending ridging through the 
eastern Plains...while the western CONUS remains under 
troughing, with the main disturbances off the west Baja coast 
and the Nrn Rockies and other weaker embedded waves. At the 
surface, not looking at an overly strong pattern across the 
region, as we sit with a large area of high pressure set up over
the Great Lakes/Northeast, and low pressure/troughing along the
High Plains. This is keeping winds across the forecast area 
south-southeasterly, with gusts at times around 20-25 MPH. Cloud
cover has been a bit of a nuisance...this morning skies were 
dominated by widespread low-level stratus. This cloud cover did 
eventually diminish from SSW to NNE (though a little still 
lingers in extreme NNE areas)...so while we have had some sun, 
this next wave is bringing more clouds right back in...so those 
SWrn areas haven't had the chance to warm quite as much as had 
hoped. Central/northern areas still have a bit of time to get 
temps to/just above the 70 degree mark. 

Tonight through Friday night...

The main story through the shorter term period through the end
of the work week continues with lie with increased 
preciptiation chances and potential for at least a couple inches
of rain in spots. Overall there hasn't been any significant 
change in the forecast...precipitation chances ramp up tonight, 
and remain fairly high (70-90 percent in spots) through this 
period...though it doesn't look to be a non-stop rainout. In the
upper levels, models aren't in too bad of agreement in the 
broader scale...showing mainly southwesterly flow across the 
region, set up between an increasingly dampened and westward 
shifting area of high pressure and continued troughing over the 
western CONUS as another larger-scale system works its way onto 
the West Coast. Models showing a couple of rounds of 
showers/storms working through the forecast area...primarly 
favoring the evening hours on into at least the first part of 
the following day. There remain plenty of uncertainties in the 
exact timing...models showing relative lulls in activity, but 
differ in exactly when they occur and how long they actually 
last for additional activity fires up/moves into the area. 

The overall threat for severe weather remains on the lower side, 
with models continuing to show not a great chance for better 
instability to work its way into the area...keeping heavy 
rainfall the main hazard. Looking at ensemble probability data, 
the EC ens remain more on the optimistic side for amounts than 
the GFS...continuing to show widespread probabilities of 80+ 
percent of at least one inch over much of the forecast area, 
though the most recent run did note a bit of a southward 
shift...and still has a decent area of probabilities of 40-70 
percent of 2 inches or more. The GFS ensemble data keeps the 
probabilities of 1+ inch more in the 40-80 percent range, with 
probability of 2+ inches confined to a narrower swath of only 
10-30 percent. Not out of the question there could be some spots
with minor hydro issues...but the fact that these totals are 
spread out and not all falling within say a 6-hr period helps.

This weekend and beyond...

Current forecast keeps the majority of the weekend dry...main  
uncertainty is on Saturday, with how long activity moving
through Friday-Friday night lingers around into the day. 
Unfortunately there are still plenty of differences to work out 
between models...some are much slower to push things out of here
than others on Saturday.

The dry forecast even continues into the start of the new work 
week...potentially through all of the daytime hours on Monday,
but that's definitely not a certainty, with some models 
showing precip already returning at some point during the 
afternoon. The better chances look to hold off further into the 
evening/overnight hours on Monday...continuing into the day on 
Tuesday as models show the next notable upper level system 
moving through. Exactly how this system evolves is uncertain, 
affecting the timing...the ECMWF is a slower, more organized 
upper low moving through, keeping precip around on into Wed...vs
the more open, progressive GFS which clears things out quicker.
Will just have to see how things trend in the coming days. 

As far as temperatures go, following 60s-70s forecast for Thu-
Fri (which may be optimistic depending on precip 
trends)...70s-low 80s
